strengths: Tackles a well-recognized and important open problem in predictive coding/equilibrium propagation research: the inability to train PC networks deeper than ~5-7 layers, which is a major obstacle to broader adoption of biologically-inspired/energy-based learning.

Provides a clear diagnostic experiment (layer-wise energy tracking, Figure 2 and appendix Figures 5-6) comparing PC to BP that visually demonstrates the energy imbalance phenomenon, giving a plausible causal narrative for the degradation.

Proposes a reasonably diverse set of complementary interventions (spiking precision, decaying precision, forward weight updates, BatchNorm freezing) each targeting different aspects of the identified problem, and shows they can be combined synergistically.

Extensive experimental evaluation across three datasets (CIFAR10, CIFAR100, Tiny ImageNet) and four depths (VGG5/7/10/15), with 5 seeds, hyperparameter search details, and thorough ablation studies isolating each component's contribution.

Achieves results that substantially close the gap with backprop on 10- and 15-layer convolutional networks, a genuinely useful empirical advance in the field (Tiny ImageNet, 15 layers) previously only reached via hybrid BP/EP training.
Good reproducibility documentation: detailed appendix with architecture specs, hyperparameter search ranges, data augmentation and normalization details, and reported training-time comparisons.
Honest limitations section acknowledging that the theoretical understanding of the energy imbalance phenomenon and the biological implausibility introduced by forward updates remain open issues.
weaknesses: The central causal claim is only partially substantiated: Figure 2 shows that even with the proposed methods, the energy imbalance remains many orders of magnitude (e.g., still ~10^-10 vs ~10^-2 for BP), yet accuracy improves substantially — the paper does not rigorously establish why partial mitigation suffices, weakening the mechanistic story to more of a correlational conjecture.

Individual components behave inconsistently across settings: e.g., in Table 2 (Tiny ImageNet), Spiking Precision alone underperforms plain PC (18.36 vs 22.95 top-1), and Decaying+Forward Update is worse than Forward Update alone (21.95 vs 31.61); these inconsistencies are not analyzed in depth and undercut confidence in the proposed mechanisms as generally reliable rather than dataset/architecture-specific tricks.

The forward-update mechanism, which contributes most to the gains, is explicitly acknowledged to reduce biological plausibility (requiring storage of initial forward predictions), which is in tension with the paper's initial motivation (neuromorphic/analog hardware and local learning) — the significance of the contribution for the stated application domain is thus weakened.

On the hardest benchmark (Tiny ImageNet, VGG15), the best proposed combination (S+F) still slightly underperforms BP (42.51 vs 44.52 top-1 without BF; 53.04 vs 53.21 with BF), so the claim of 'comparable to backprop' is only approximately true and the paper's D+F variant is notably worse.

No empirical comparison to other recent approaches addressing depth in PC/EP models (e.g., hybrid BP/EP models, or the contemporaneous μPC method cited only in the conclusion), making it hard to judge how this method compares to alternative state-of-the-art solutions to the same problem.

The precision-weighting schemes (spiking, decaying) are heuristic constructions without theoretical grounding for why these particular functional forms should rebalance energy correctly; no principled derivation or convergence guarantee is provided.

Minor presentation issues (e.g., 'BarchNorm' typo, dense notation, some figures with small unlabeled text) slightly reduce clarity, and the energy-imbalance-vanishing-gradient analogy is asserted rather than formally connected.

strengths: Addresses an important and underexplored problem: why predictive coding networks (PCNs) trained with EP-like local learning degrade sharply beyond 5-7 layers, which is directly relevant to the broader EP/PC and neuromorphic-hardware community.

The layer-wise energy visualization (Fig. 2, Fig. 5) comparing BP and PC during training is a useful diagnostic contribution that helps make the 'energy imbalance' hypothesis concrete and visually compelling.

Extensive empirical evaluation across multiple architectures (VGG5/7/10/15), datasets (CIFAR-10/100, Tiny ImageNet) and a fairly large hyperparameter search (TPE, 500 iterations) with 5 seeds, which is commendable for reproducibility within the PC/EP line of work.
Reasonably thorough ablation study isolating the contribution of each proposed component (precision schemes, forward update, BatchNorm Freezing).
The connection to neuroscientific precision-weighting is a conceptually interesting motivation, even if the proposed schedules end up being largely heuristic.
weaknesses: The central causal claim ('energy imbalance causes degradation, and our precision methods fix it by re-balancing energy') is not well supported: the paper itself admits the proposed precision methods 'slightly mitigate' the imbalance 'despite it being still very significant' (Sec 4), yet the abstract and conclusion claim this confirms a causal relationship. The evidence is correlational at best.

The individual precision methods (Spiking, Decaying) frequently underperform plain PC when used alone, in both CIFAR and Tiny ImageNet experiments (e.g., VGG7/CIFAR10: PC=84.62 vs S=82.16, D=81.14; Tiny ImageNet Top-1: PC=22.95 vs S=18.36), directly undermining the narrative that precision-weighting addresses the diagnosed bottleneck. The paper does not reconcile this inconsistency convincingly.

Most of the empirical gains appear to be driven by the 'Forward Update' mechanism (and BatchNorm Freezing) rather than the precision-weighting schemes that are the paper's main theoretical contribution; the precision mechanisms seem to contribute marginally and inconsistently, weakening the claimed significance of the core idea.

The Forward Update mechanism explicitly increases biological implausibility (storing initialization-time predictions in memory for later use), which cuts against the paper's own motivation (local, hardware-/brain-plausible learning) stated in the introduction — this tension is acknowledged but not resolved.

The proposed precision schedules (Eq. 4-5) are ad hoc engineering constructions (hand-tuned spikes/decays tied to iteration/layer indices) rather than being derived from a principled objective; there is no theoretical analysis of why these particular functional forms should balance energy, only empirical curve-fitting post hoc.

Computational cost is substantial and likely underplayed: PCNs require ~8-10x longer per epoch than BP (Table 6) due to the need for T relaxation iterations scaling with depth, which is a serious practical limitation for scaling to 'complex tasks' as claimed in the abstract, yet this is relegated to an appendix with a reassuring but unconvincing explanation (implementation bottleneck).

Comparisons are limited to vanilla PC and BP as baselines; no empirical comparison is made to directly competing recent depth-scaling approaches for PC/EP (e.g., the contemporaneous μPC work cited in the conclusion, or the hybrid BP+EP model of Nest and Ernoult 2024 that already trained 15-layer models), making it hard to assess the actual advance over the state of the art.

The full method requires stacking four separate heuristic components (precision scheme + forward update + BatchNorm Freezing + specific optimizer/schedule choices), each contributing inconsistently across settings (per the ablation), which raises concerns about overfitting to the specific benchmarks tested and about the generality/robustness of the approach.

Presentation is dense and notation-heavy (e.g., the precision/covariance formalism, Fig. 1) which could be streamlined; some empirical claims are stated more strongly in prose than the accompanying numbers justify (e.g., 'performances comparable to those of backprop' despite several gaps and inconsistent orderings across tables).

strengths: Addresses a timely and important problem: the well-documented failure of predictive coding/EP networks to scale beyond 5-7 layers, which is a major obstacle for the biologically-plausible learning community.

The empirical diagnosis of layer-wise energy imbalance (Figure 2, Figure 5) is a clear and useful contribution; comparing energy/error magnitudes across layers between BP and PC provides intuitive evidence for the proposed mechanism.

The proposed methods (spiking precision, decaying precision, forward updates, BatchNorm freezing) are simple, hyperparameter-light (spiking precision adds none), and easy to integrate into existing PC pipelines.

Extensive experimental evaluation across CIFAR-10/100 and Tiny ImageNet, multiple VGG depths (5/7/10/15), with 5-seed averages and large hyperparameter searches (500 TPE iterations), indicating a thorough empirical effort.
Achieves a notable milestone: training a 15-layer convolutional PC network on Tiny ImageNet with accuracy close to BP, a depth previously reachable only via hybrid BP+EP schemes.
Good reproducibility: detailed architecture tables, hyperparameter search ranges, training schedule, and computational cost comparisons are provided in the appendix.
Thorough ablation study isolating the contribution of each proposed component and their interactions.
weaknesses: The causal story is only partially supported: the paper itself acknowledges the energy imbalance is 'still very significant' even with the proposed fixes (Section 4), so the link between the diagnosed mechanism and the performance gains remains correlational rather than fully demonstrated.

The functional forms for spiking and decaying precision appear heuristically chosen (e.g., spike exactly at l = L-t, specific exponential decay form) rather than derived from a principled objective; no theoretical analysis explains why these specific schedules are optimal or necessary.

Ablation results are inconsistent: individual components (D, S, or F alone) sometimes underperform standard PC (e.g., Decaying Precision alone on VGG7/CIFAR10 is 81.14% vs. PC's 84.62%; D+F on Tiny ImageNet Top-1 without BF is 21.95% vs. PC's 22.95%), suggesting the gains are highly dependent on specific combinations rather than robust standalone mechanisms.

The forward-update mechanism explicitly sacrifices biological plausibility (requires storing initialization predictions), which undermines part of the original motivation for using PC/EP as a biologically-plausible, hardware-friendly alternative to BP.

No comparison to the contemporaneous μPC work (Innocenti et al. 2025), which reportedly addresses similar scaling issues theoretically; the significance of the proposed approach relative to this competing method is unclear.

The paper conflates equilibrium propagation and predictive coding somewhat loosely in the introduction/title despite the technical content being entirely about predictive coding, which could mislead readers about the scope of applicability.
Some high-variance results (e.g., PC on VGG10/CIFAR10: 72.75±6.03) raise concerns about the stability of baselines and whether reported improvements are robust to this variance.
Experiments are restricted to VGG-style CNNs; no evidence yet that the proposed fixes generalize to residual or transformer-based architectures, which are explicitly left to future work.
